clue.text: It might secure a piece of garlic to thumb?

parts.note: a single segment of a garlic bulb is a clove
to thumb a lift is to hitch one, so thumb means hitch

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether a garlic segment could be fastened to their thumb.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the silly picture; the definition is the knot, a sailor's hitch made with two turns round a post or rope.
explanation.definitionFit: A clove hitch is a common knot used to fasten a rope to a spar or post.

clue.text: Rope and flag put out for children's fun

indicators.note: put out suggests the letters are disturbed and thrown into disorder, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: Rope and a flag are set out ready for a children's game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put out' rearranges ROPE and FLAG together.
explanation.definitionFit: Leapfrog is a playground game where children vault over each other's bent backs.

clue.text: Check old soldier

definitions.meaning: to examine or screen something carefully
short for veteran, a former serviceman

explanation.definitionFit: To vet is to scrutinise, and a vet is also a veteran, someone who has served in the forces.

clue.text: Drug an animal in the gym

definitions.meaning: the vaulting apparatus in a gymnasium is called a ..., a joke on it being an animal

explanation.definitionFit: Horse is slang for heroin, and the padded vaulting box in a gymnasium shares the name of the farm animal.

clue.text: During Macbeth eat refinedly here?

indicators.note: During says the letters run through the middle of the words that follow, held within them

explanation.surface: Asks whether one might dine politely during a performance of Macbeth.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition: Macbeth is a play, and the place to see it is where the letters sit inside 'Macbeth eat refinedly'.
explanation.definitionFit: A playhouse is where Macbeth would be staged, so the whole clue points to it.

clue.text: After an hour at work put an end to game

indicators.note: After places the piece for at work following the piece for an hour

parts.note: H is the standard abbreviation for hour
OP is short for operation, so on op means working
to scotch a rumour or plan is to put an end to it

explanation.surface: After an hour on the job, someone calls a halt to a game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After' puts OP (at work, in operation) after H (hour); OP is a crossword convention for working, as in 'in operation'.
explanation.definitionFit: Hopscotch is a children's playground game of hopping through chalked squares.

clue.text: Stop daughter following poet

indicators.note: following places the piece for daughter after the piece for stop

parts.note: to bar is to stop or block
D is the usual abbreviation for daughter in family trees

explanation.surface: A father prevents his daughter from going after a poet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'following' puts D after BAR.
explanation.definitionFit: A bard is a poet, and Shakespeare is known as the Bard.

clue.text: Lying to look good?

parts.note: lying is lying down in bed, not telling untruths: rest taken to improve one's looks

explanation.walkthrough: 'Lying' suggests telling fibs to appear virtuous; it means lying asleep, the rest said to keep one attractive.
explanation.definitionFit: Extra sleep, supposedly taken to keep a person looking fresh and attractive, is the idiom here.

clue.text: About to arrange a place for holidaymakers to go to

definitions.text: a place for holidaymakers to go to

parts.note: RE is Latin for about or concerning, as in business letters
to sort is to arrange or put in order

explanation.surface: Someone is about to book a holiday destination.
explanation.definitionFit: A seaside or ski town that people visit for holidays is a resort.

clue.text: Irish writer consumed gold drink

indicators.note: consumed means the writer's name has swallowed the other piece, holding it inside

parts.note: Laurence Sterne, author of Tristram Shandy, was born in Ireland
AU is the chemical symbol for gold

explanation.surface: An Irish author drank down a golden drink.
explanation.walkthrough: Laurence Sterne, author of Tristram Shandy, was born in Clonmel, Ireland, which makes him the Irish writer; 'consumed' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Sauterne is a sweet white dessert wine from Bordeaux.

clue.text: Commend leader of psychiatrists at institute

indicators.note: leader of picks the first letter of the word psychiatrists

parts.note: to raise something, such as an objection or an action, is to institute or set it up

explanation.surface: Praise for the head of psychiatry at a research institute.
explanation.walkthrough: 'institute' looks like a noun naming the workplace; it is a verb, to set up or raise.
explanation.definitionFit: To commend is to speak well of someone, which is to praise them.

clue.text: Where many of us work is where winter sportsmen relax?

definitions.meaning: skaters or hockey players resting are off the ice

explanation.definitionFit: Many people work in an office, and the word read as two parts is where skaters rest: away from the rink.

clue.text: Assume character's no spare time when busy

indicators.note: when busy suggests the letters are bustling about, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone with no free time pretends to be somebody else.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when busy' rearranges NO SPARE TIME; the 's is a link meaning 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: To assume a character is to play the part of another person, to pose as them.

clue.text: Reserved one act after another one failed

indicators.note: after places the piece for one act following the other pieces
failed suggests things falling apart, so these letters are jumbled

parts.note: another means another act, carrying over the act already named
one is the Roman numeral I
a turn is a single act on a variety bill

explanation.surface: A performance falls flat after the previous one also bombed, leaving the audience quiet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'failed' jumbles ACT and I into TACI; 'after' then puts TURN (one act on a variety bill) after it. 'another' stands for another act.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone reserved says little, which is to be taciturn or uncommunicative.

clue.text: Sound from common pest is funny

indicators.note: funny means odd or peculiar, so these letters are put in a strange order

explanation.surface: Something sounds as though it comes from a household pest that is comical.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sound' is the definition, meaning sane, not a noise; 'funny' rearranges COMMON PEST IS.
explanation.definitionFit: Of sound mind is Latin compos mentis, meaning in full possession of one's mental faculties.

clue.text: Insurance policy a top performer may require in the event of a fall

definitions.meaning: a fallback arrangement guarding against failure

definitions.text: a top performer may require in the event of a fall
definitions.meaning: a trapeze artist high up needs a mesh stretched below to catch them

explanation.definitionFit: A fallback safeguard is figuratively one, and literally it is the mesh below a high-wire act.

clue.text: Way to encourage producer of expensive eggs

parts.note: ST is the abbreviation for street, a way
to urge on is to encourage

explanation.surface: A method of spurring on a hen that lays costly eggs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to' is a link; the eggs are caviar.
explanation.definitionFit: Caviar, a luxury food, is the roe of this large fish.

clue.text: Note new students with extremely tasteless snacks etc

parts.note: RE is the second note of the sol-fa scale
first-year university students are freshmen

indicators.note: extremely picks the letters at the extremes of tasteless, its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A notice says the new students' snacks are terribly bland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'extremely' gives TS, the first and last letters of 'tasteless'.
explanation.definitionFit: Light food and drink served at an event are refreshments.

clue.text: Hearing 4 with a temperature playing

indicators.note: playing suggests the letters frolic about, so they are mixed up

parts.note: 4 points to the answer of the clue numbered 4, the drug and gym animal

explanation.surface: A feverish horse is playing about within hearing distance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'playing' rearranges HORSE (the answer to 4), A and T.
explanation.definitionFit: Within earshot means within hearing range, the distance a sound can be heard.

clue.text: I left after fast pulse

indicators.note: after places the pieces for I and left following the piece for fast

parts.note: Lent is the Christian period of fasting before Easter

explanation.surface: Someone departed after a fasting period, perhaps with a heartbeat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pulse' looks like a heartbeat; it is the edible seed of a legume.
explanation.definitionFit: A pulse is an edible legume seed, such as a pea, bean or lentil.

clue.text: Journo about to have beer

parts.note: RE means about or concerning
porter is a dark beer

explanation.surface: A journalist is about to have a beer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to have' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Journo is informal for a journalist, such as a news correspondent.

clue.text: Excellent drink at the queen at start of binge

parts.note: to sup is to drink
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the Queen

indicators.note: start of picks the first letter of the word binge

explanation.surface: Drinking with the Queen at the beginning of a binge is splendid.
explanation.walkthrough: ER stands for Elizabeth Regina, the Queen; 'at the' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Superb means of the highest quality, splendid.

clue.text: Prisoner skips soup for a bloody fight

indicators.note: skips means the prisoner's piece is left out of the soup

parts.note: consomme is a clear soup
CON is short for convict, a prisoner

explanation.surface: A prisoner goes without soup, prompting a violent brawl.
explanation.walkthrough: 'skips' removes CON (convict) from CONSOMME; the Somme was a costly First World War battle.
explanation.definitionFit: The Battle of the Somme in 1916 was among the bloodiest engagements of the First World War.

clue.text: Filter natural water from small stone

parts.note: ST is the abbreviation for stone, the unit of weight
rain is water that falls naturally

explanation.surface: Instructions to filter natural water away from small pebbles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'small stone' is the abbreviation ST, not a pebble; 'from' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To filter liquid through a sieve is to strain it.

clue.text: The house beer?

parts.note: a home is a house or dwelling
a brew is a beer, as in a pint of the local brew

explanation.walkthrough: A 'house beer' suggests a bar's own brand; the question mark points to beer made in someone's own house, and the whole clue defines it.
explanation.definitionFit: Ale or beer made by amateurs in their own kitchen is the sense.

clue.text: Show disapproval of tedious type right away

indicators.note: away means the letter for right is taken out

parts.note: a boor is a coarse, tiresome person

explanation.surface: Someone disapproves of a dull person immediately.
explanation.walkthrough: 'right away' looks like 'at once'; it means remove R from BOOR.
explanation.definitionFit: To jeer at a performer by shouting is to express disapproval of them.

clue.text: Reminder left inside — one of 28 here

indicators.note: inside means the piece for left goes within the piece for reminder

parts.note: a cue is a prompt or reminder

explanation.surface: A reminder is left inside one of the puzzle's twenty-eight entries.
explanation.walkthrough: This puzzle has 28 clues, and the answer is one of them.
explanation.definitionFit: This puzzle contains 28 cryptic hints, so the answer names any one of them.

clue.text: What's rude about article is relevant

indicators.note: about means the rude phrase goes around the article

parts.note: as children are told, it's rude to point
THE is the definite article

explanation.surface: Asks what is rude about an article, as relevant commentary.
explanation.walkthrough: The writer relies on the nursery reproof 'it's rude to point', so the phrase stands for what is rude; 'about' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Relevant remarks are apposite and pertinent, sticking closely to the matter.
